audit.whatIsWrong: 2+ items was scored for Sion while whys[6], spikes[3] and the late paragraph all say the opposite — 'the more tank items he buys, the more stats you steal' and 'Frozen Domain traps him for the entire drain cycle'.
audit.why: Trundle is at 54.74% over 380 games, the largest sample in the slice, and the way he wins is by out-scaling a tank into the side lane. Scoring the stage where that happens for Sion inverts the whole point of the matchup.
audit.corrected: 2+ items moved to Trundle in both layers. Chart now reads Trundle / Skill / Sion / Sion / Trundle / Sion / Trundle — three Trundle stages against a 54.74% win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every Subjugate figure in the matchup is invented, and they contradict each other: '25% of his Armor and MR' in spikes[1] and whys[4] and mid, '12.5%' in wants.you[2], 'the full 50%' in whys[6], and 'a 200-armor Sion becomes a 170-armor Sion' in late — which is 15%, a fourth number.
audit.why: Four different percentages for one ability inside one matchup, none of which appear in Riot's text. Subjugate's description gives a percent steal that doubles over the next 4 seconds and nothing else. The player is being asked to size his entire level-6 plan against a number the page made up.
audit.corrected: All five replaced with the stated mechanic — a percent of health, armour and MR on cast, doubling over the following 4 seconds — plus Subjugate's real 120/100/80s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a Sion ability (packet defect) and misses two effects that decide the lane. Roar of the Slayer REDUCES ARMOR on the first enemy hit — he shreds back exactly what Subjugate just stole, and the matchup calls it only 'E poke'. Glory in Death makes his post-death attacks HEAL HIM and deal bonus damage based on your MAXIMUM HEALTH, so armour and health stacking are both wrong answers to the zombie. Chomp is also called an attack-SPEED steal in five fields; it saps attack damage.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point. The armour shred is a direct counter to your ultimate and appears nowhere; the zombie's max-health scaling and self-heal are why Grievous Wounds is your first back, which the itemization line already recommends without ever saying why.
audit.corrected: Decimating Smash, Soul Furnace, Roar of the Slayer, Unstoppable Onslaught and Glory in Death all named with cooldowns; the armour shred and the zombie's heal-plus-max-health damage stated; the sap corrected to attack damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: early tells you to re-engage 'after the 12-second cooldown' on his shield. Soul Furnace is 15/14/13/12/11s — 12 seconds is its rank-4 value, and at level 2 it is 15.
audit.why: The whole level-2 plan is 'bait the shield, come back when it is down'. Coming back three seconds early walks into a fresh shield.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 15s at rank 1, and the 3-second reactivation window on Soul Furnace added, since that is the beat where the shield turns into damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'He has no dash or gap-closer to escape Pillar of Ice' in the level-6 paragraph — the same paragraph where he unlocks Unstoppable Onslaught, a steerable charge with 7500 range.
audit.why: It is true before 6 and false from 6 onward, and the sentence sits in the level-6 section. The knock-up also scales with how far he has charged, which is the actual handle on it.
audit.corrected: Kept the no-dash point where it belongs (levels 1-5) and replaced the level-6 version with the real read: meet the charge early, before the distance bonus builds.

edits.before: Level 1 is a chess match of short trades: your Chomp Q steals attack speed and heals off any dying minion, but Sion can cancel your advantage by charging his Q before you close — if you see him standing still and winding up, walk sideways, don't chase. At level 2 he gets his W shield online and will try to block your first Chomp damage with it; bait him into pre-popping the shield on a weak trade, then immediately go for a second Chomp sequence after the 12-second cooldown — you win that window cleanly. At level 3 his Q knockup, W shield, and E shatter-poke are all live, and that is genuinely his best 1v1 window in this lane: if he lands the charged knockup, he wins the trade decisively. Stay at medium range, bait the Q channel by feinting in, then sidestep and punish his recovery with Chomp into Frozen Domain.
edits.after: Level 1 is a chess match of short trades: Chomp saps his attack damage and King's Tribute heals off any dying minion, but Sion cancels that advantage by charging Decimating Smash before you close — if you see him standing still and winding up, walk sideways, do not chase. At level 2 Soul Furnace comes online and he will try to eat your first Chomp with it; bait the shield out on a weak trade, then re-engage on its 15-second rank-1 cooldown and you win that window cleanly. At level 3 the charged knock-up, the shield and Roar of the Slayer are all live, and that is genuinely his best 1v1 window in this lane — Roar also reduces your armour on the first target it hits. Stay at medium range, feint in to bait the charge, sidestep it, then punish the recovery with Chomp into Frozen Domain.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 bring the lane back toward even — your Frozen Domain movement and healing are harder for an immobile Sion to escape, and Chomp's cumulative AS steal in a long trade punishes him for standing and fighting on his own terms. Don't all-in when his W shield is healthy; instead, use Pillar of Ice to cut off his escape route toward tower, force him to fight inside your ice, and let your passive King's Tribute heal off every caster minion death to undo his E poke. Level 6 shifts things back in your favor: pop Subjugate the moment you engage — the instant 25% Armor and MR drain means his armor is now partly your armor, and combined with Frozen Domain's attack speed steroid, your Chomp autos outdamage his basic attacks in a straight brawl. He has no dash or gap-closer to escape Pillar of Ice, so once you drop the pillar behind him the kill becomes straightforward.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 bring the lane back toward even — Frozen Domain's movement and healing are hard for an immobile Sion to escape, and Chomp's attack-damage sap punishes him for standing and fighting. He has no dash before 6, so Pillar of Ice behind him takes the retreat outright. Do not all-in into a healthy Soul Furnace; bait it, and note he can reactivate it after 3 seconds for damage. Level 6 shifts back to you: cast Subjugate as you engage, because the percent it takes from his health, armour and MR doubles over the next 4 seconds and his armour becomes yours for the fight. His answer is Roar of the Slayer, which reduces armour on the first target hit, so expect some of it back. Unstoppable Onslaught is now his gap-closer too, and the knock-up scales with how far he has charged — meet it early rather than letting it build.

edits.before: At two items, Sion becomes the most Subjugate-friendly target imaginable: every Warmog, Heartsteel, or Frozen Heart stack he buys directly increases how much Armor and MR you strip with the double-cast ultimate, turning his own itemization into a liability. Keep Frozen Domain placed in the 1v1 zone, Chomp repeatedly to shred his attack speed, and save Pillar of Ice for when he tries to retreat toward his tower wall. In teamfights your R drain on their front-line Sion is one of the highest-value ultimates in the game — a 200-armor Sion becomes a 170-armor Sion and a 200-armor Trundle at the same time. Respect the zombie passive: if you blow your combo killing him and his spirit form keeps fighting, kite back under Frozen Domain and finish it with one or two Chomp autos before the timer expires.
edits.after: At two items Sion becomes the most Subjugate-friendly target imaginable: every Warmog, Heartsteel or Frozen Heart he buys deepens the stat pool your ultimate takes a percent of, and the theft doubles over the following 4 seconds, turning his own itemization into a liability. Keep Frozen Domain placed in the 1v1 zone, Chomp repeatedly to sap his attack damage, and save Pillar of Ice for the moment he walks back toward his tower. In teamfights, draining the front-line Sion is one of the highest-value ultimates in the game — his resistances move onto you for the whole fight. Respect Glory in Death as well: the zombie's attacks heal him and scale off your maximum health, so armour and HP stacking both feed it, and Grievous Wounds is what actually shortens it.
